column5: If means only when something happens (false, if is not only when) => If tells us what must happen first; also .002 and .007
But joins opposite ideas. => But joins ideas that are different.
A dictionary does not tell us who first said a word. => A dictionary does not usually tell us who first said a word.
Which letter comes after m (o and p also come after m) => comes right after m
hint Between a and o, but cave has second letter a => look at the third letter too; explanation now gives both reasons
Short words take -er (more fun, more real) => Short words like big take -er
consonant + y always changes to i (shy, shyer) => usually; also er-est.807
one vowel and one last consonant doubles (low, new do not) => one short vowel
never put more in front of an -er word (more clever, more eager) => a comparing word like higher
Big has one vowel and one consonant (it has two consonants) => one short vowel and ends in one consonant; hint Short words double (long, fast) => like big
True or false: hottest has two t letters, keyed True, and hottest has three => has a double t in the middle; hint Count the ts => look after the o
Too means also, or very (too hot is not very hot) => also, or more than is needed
A herd is a group of cows => a group of animals, such as cows; also .012
Knight is a man who rode a horse. => A knight was a soldier who rode a horse.
keyed option said the Moon changes shape => seems to change shape, explanation too
Titles tell us what a text is about. => Titles often tell us what a text is about.
prompt asked about children, the picture shows one child => the child, hint too
Describe what the animals are doing, the icons show no action => Say what each animal might be doing
We only add -es after s, sh, ch, x or z (false: tomatoes, potatoes) => Cat ends in t, so it just adds -s; same note in .005
Words ending in s, sh, ch, x, z add -es (stomachs) => Most words; .002 .004 .006 .801 .804
spell babies, hint said It does not end in s => It does not end in ys
Strawberry has two r letters (it has three, and the wrong label strawbery has two) => The berry part has two
ready: covering re leaves ady, note said Dy => Ady
untidy, hint Three letters plus tidy, un has two => Two letters
Un- and dis- mean not, in an item with unpack => often mean not
words that mean not => words with a prefix that means not, explanation too
The first spoken word always starts with a capital letter => The first spoken word starts with a capital letter
These are only the first word. => This is only the first word.
groups Has speech / Has no speech, but Dina said hello does report speech => Has speech marks / No speech marks
spoken words followed by said take a comma (questions and exclamations do not) => spoken words that tell something
rubric asks for speech marks, model had none => one line of speech added, also .012
This comes in the middle. => This usually comes later in the story.
Sighed shows a breath of tiredness. => Sighed shows a long breath, not a loud voice.
Use at least two speech marks. => Use speech marks at least twice.
-ly tells how (friendly, lovely) => often tells how; .005 .017
consonant + y changes before -ly and -ful (shyly) => usually; .006 .012 .805
all words in -le change -le to -ly (solely, palely) => words like gentle and simple, many words
Peaceless is not a word, and it does not tell how. => Peaceless would mean without peace, and it does not tell how.
Use without something is useless. => Something with no use is useless.
When the suffix -ful starts with a consonant, the silent e stays. => The suffix -ful starts with a consonant, so the silent e in hope stays.
Brave means not afraid (brave people can be afraid) => ready to face danger; opposite hint too
Warm, boiling and scorching are hot. Chilly, freezing and icy are cold. => Warm, boiling and scorching go with hot. Chilly, freezing and icy go with cold.
not about movement: sleep is not movement either, two answers => not a doing word, why notes too
hint Think of the lion, no lion anywhere => the saying as brave as a lion
They both mean very sad => They both mean sad
Am needs an -ing word (I am happy) => With visit, am needs -ing
on Sunday, today is Monday: will go and are going fit the coming Sunday => yesterday, on Sunday
Sing and eat change their whole word. => Sing and eat do not add ed.
Present tense verbs tell us what is happening now. => Present tense verbs can tell us what is happening now.
The cover only shows the title. => The cover does not list the topics in the book.
A story is made up. => Many stories are made up.
why on Mina eats beans and Mina likes mornings said only one detail, the text says neither => The text does not say that
An adverb tells more about a verb (very big, very quickly) => can tell; .001 .029 .031
A preposition tells where (on Monday, with a pen) => can tell; .002 .017 .021 .802 .805
Between needs two things, as in between the trees => things on each side
fronted adverbial is followed by a comma (short ones may have none, Today we played) => usually; .022 .803
A comma follows an adverbial only when it comes first => usually follows, when it comes first
at the end of the lane describes the shop here, why called it an adverbial inside the sentence => starts with its subject, not an adverbial
Can't is can not squashed together. => Can't is a short form of cannot.
Apostrophe before s means one owner (children's), after s means more than one (James') => Here, in .801 and .802
Times, numbers and lists are facts. => Times, numbers and lists can be checked.
capital of Indonesia example may go out of date with the move to Nusantara => Jakarta is a city on the island of Java
Opinions are feelings. => Opinions show what someone thinks or feels.
planning What can or cannot you do? (not English word order) => What can you do, and what can you not do?
hints named Class 4B and Mrs Wulan, a letter the child cannot see => a letter asking a head teacher for something
hint named a school garden news report the child cannot see => a news report you have read
Leaf and loaf end in f, so f changes (roof, chef do not) => Like many words ending in f; .001 .004
Words in x, s, sh, ch add -es (stomachs) => Most words; .015 .018
hint One animal stays the same, deer and sheep both do => Some animal words
mice called farm animals => animals on a farm
pony: letter before y is n, hint named P and n => N is a consonant
The walkers slipped, so the path was not pretty. => Slipping tells us nothing about how pretty the path was.
keyed sentence said magma poured from the crater; out of the ground it is lava => lava, hint and explanation too
There is no like or as, so it is a metaphor, not a simile. => There is no like or as. It says the snow was a blanket, so it is a metaphor, not a simile.
Owls hunt at night (some hunt by day), food never hears them => most of them, food rarely hears them
An exclamation mark shows surprise. => An exclamation mark shows strong feeling.
comma after speech marks (it goes inside) => Inside; hint A sentence cannot have a question mark and a comma together => should not sit side by side
hint The word rat hides the letters a, r and a (rat has r, a, t) => a rat hides inside: sep, a, rat, e
why said only believe ends with e, piece does too => Field and chief do not; i before e now a rule that often works
explanation said the last sentence uses all three, the keyed one is first and the last is wrong => names the sentence; hint Try the last sentence first => Test each sentence the same way
Have does not go with one person (I have, you have) => not with she
consonant + y changes before -ness (shyness, dryness) => usually; .010 .803
story, recipe and letter openings stated as always => often, usually, many
It links the cause (a flat tyre) to what happened next. => It links the cause (running) to what happened next.
Bats use sound to find food (fruit bats mostly do not) => Many bats; also .042
Buying needs was or were, not has. => Buying needs a helper like is or was, not has.
eaten called the past form of eat (that is ate) => After has, the form is eaten; .806 now a past form such as seen or gone
watered also fits the sentence => prompt now asks for the verb that shows the action was still going on
gap While he ___ along the path: walked is also correct English and was marked wrong => option walked replaced by walks
The ending -ian means a person => The ending -ian here means a person
In bicycle, bi means two wheels. => In bicycle, bi means two.
carefully: one l was dropped from -ful (none is) => two l letters, one from -ful and one from -ly
gap ___ it was cold, we went swimming: Until it was cold also makes sense => option Until replaced by Or
Say where the things are, the icons show no places => Say where you would put these things
Letters begin with a greeting and end with a goodbye => Most letters begin with a greeting and end with a goodbye
gap sentence read My two dogs dogs' bowls are empty when filled => My two ___ bowls are empty
Capital letters are only needed at the start (names too) => do not all need capital letters
The first paragraph gives a problem. The second gives an action. => Paragraph 2 gives a problem. Paragraph 3 gives an action.
gap 2 and 3 options capitalised mid sentence (carry Their bags) => lower case
contest-style items outside their skill (ie/ei spelling in homophones, compound words in suffixes, analogies in synonyms), true but off-skill, not moved
